finding.before: All three text-to-SymPy paths call parse_expr. Controlled statements invoke a Python hook in memory, including a module name built from chr calls that passes the former character filter. Unknown identifiers can also be silently interpreted as products of symbols, attributes as Python classes, decimals as Float.
finding.after: One closed arithmetic grammar constructs mathematical objects directly. Exact declared names, rational literals, + - * / powers, parentheses, implicit multiplication, and the fixed sqrt constructor are the only productions. No evaluated Python string, attribute access, arbitrary callable, auto-created symbol or parse_expr remains. The extrema family accepts only actual univariate polynomials.

tests.scope: Controlled mathematical and memory-only fixtures. No current QCM or published program executed.

memory_probes.effect: Only append to a test list and return a SymPy expression; no filesystem operation or network request in evaluated payload.

grammar_limits.meaning: Supported reader complexity bounds; expressions outside this subset remain unproved, never omitted from the QCM corpus.

method_binding: Implementation remains within qcm_independent_solver.py, already tracked by QA010. No new source dependency was introduced.
not_run: Global V2 replay/generation until independent parser review.

independent_review.read_scope: Complete parser implementation, all three call sites and preprocessing, all 49 parser fixtures, and QA010 binding fixtures. Direct constructors and declared-symbol lookups are the only text-driven productions; symbol followed by parentheses multiplies rather than invoking the symbol.
independent_review.conclusion: The three identified Python-call surfaces are removed and controlled hostile syntax is rejected. Supported arithmetic fixtures preserve exact rationals and usual power/unary precedence.
